transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well. I guess I've just been feeling... wound up lately. Pretty much all day. It's just this feeling like my body is bracing for something... even when I'm just sitting at my computer, or... trying to relax after dinner. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you experienced any episodes where you felt an intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
No, I... I don't think so. It's just a constant feeling. Not really a sudden peak like that.
Do you have any recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?
No... I don't think so. Just the usual worrying, I guess. Nothing specific that gets stuck like that.
Have you been avoiding any activities or places because of your wound-up feeling?
Um... no, not really. I still go to work and... do what I need to do. I don't think I avoid anything. I just... feel tense while I'm doing it, I guess.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind?
I... didn't you just ask me that? No, I don't... I don't have thoughts that repeat like that. Just the worrying.
Do you feel compelled to perform any specific rituals or behaviors?
Um... no. I don't do anything like that. Just... normal things, I suppose. There aren't any rituals or... whatever you mean by that.
Is there something in particular that you're worried about?

I suppose it's... not really one specific thing. My mind just sort of keeps going from one concern to another. Like... thinking about my sister in Arecibo, or... worrying if I missed something at the office. 

Then it's my husband driving home, or the bills, or church commitments... I just find myself preparing for problems that haven't even happened yet. It's just... a lot of everyday things, really.
Do you experience any physical symptoms like tremors, sweating, or rapid heartbeat when you feel wound up?
No... I don't think so. I haven't noticed any shaking or sweating. It's not really like that.
Do you think your worrying is worse than would be expected for the situations you're dealing with?

Um... I'm not really sure. I suppose... maybe? I mean, they are real things to take care of, so... I haven't really thought about what would be expected. It's just... how I've been dealing with things, I guess. I don't know.
Do you think your worrying is interfering with your daily life?

I mean... I'm still getting my work done. I still go to church, and I'm there for my family. But... I suppose it takes me a bit longer to finish my reports at work. I just... I double-check things more than I used to. And... well, I have had to apologize a few times lately for being a little short with people. But I'm still doing everything I need to do.
Have you noticed any strain in your relationships with family or friends due to your worrying?
No... not really. Things are fine with my family. I mean... we get along like we always do, so... no. I haven't noticed any strain.
How long have you been feeling this wound-up sensation?
Um... I guess it's been about thirteen months now. It started around the time my sister... she lives in Arecibo... she started needing a lot more help from the family. So, since then, I suppose.
Have you felt like your worrying has affected your social life or how you interact with friends outside of family?
No... I don't think so. I mean, I still see my friends when I have the time. So... no, I haven't really noticed a difference.
Do you think your worrying is out of proportion to the actual problems you're facing?
I don't really know... I haven't thought about it like that. I mean, the things I worry about are real, so... it just feels like normal worrying to me, I guess.
Has your wound-up feeling affected your enjoyment of hobbies or leisure activities?
Um... no, not really. I still do the same things I usually do... when I have the time. So, no, I wouldn't say it's affected that.
Has your worrying affected your sleep in any way?

Well... I suppose it has, a little. I mean, most nights I do fall asleep eventually. But... I tend to wake up around three or four in the morning. My mind just starts going over things... like my sister's next appointment, or... some server issue at work. And then, even if I technically get enough hours of sleep, I just... I start the morning feeling like I never really rested at all.
Do you feel like your worrying is affecting your ability to concentrate at work?

Um... I don't think so. I mean, I'm still getting my work done. I still show up for my family, and church, and everything. 

I guess... maybe it takes me a little longer to finish reports right now. I just find myself double-checking things a bit more than I used to. And... well, I suppose I have had to apologize for sounding a little short with people I care about lately. But... I'm still doing what I need to do.
Have you had to make any significant changes to your daily routine because of your worrying?

Um... no. Like I was just saying, I haven't really changed my schedule at all. I'm still doing everything I normally do... I haven't stopped going to work or church, and I'm still showing up for my family. 

My routine is the same. It just... maybe takes a bit more effort to get through it. Like I mentioned, I'm double-checking my work a lot more, which slows down those reports. And... I guess I'm just trying to be more careful so I don't have to keep apologizing for snapping at people. But no, I haven't made any big changes to my day.
Do you think you worry more than other people about everyday things?

I... I don't know about other people. I just... I suppose my mind does stay pretty busy. 

It just sort of... jumps around. Like, I'll be thinking about my sister down in Arecibo, and then I'm wondering if I left a gap in the server logs at the office... and then I'm watching the clock, hoping my husband is okay driving home. And then there's the church committee, and the bills... 

I just... I guess I spend a lot of time trying to figure out what to do if things go wrong. Even if they... haven't. But I don't know if that's more than anyone else.
